text:
jamal: FYI support escalation from Acme — p99 on /v1/generate jumped to ~12s since 06:30 UTC. Customer filed ticket #7891. They say it looks correlated with cold/prefix misses. cc @eva @liam

eva: looking at the dashboards now. kv-prefix miss rate spiked ~8x and eviction_rate shot up. p95 also drifting. Do we have repro steps from the customer or traces?

liam: I pulled traces. Repro we used locally: generate a high-cardinality set of prompts that include user-specific tokens. Quick harness example:
```bash
# simple curl loop to emulate high prefix entropy
for i in $(seq 1 10000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"User-${i} please summarize: hello world","max_tokens":32}' > /dev/null &
done
wait
```

jamal: Customer said they rolled out a templating change that injects user IDs into the prompt body (per-user prefixes). That would blow up prefix cardinality. Could be a key normalization bug too.

cami: Remember the normalize change last week? PR #4527 modified prefix canonicalization. It stripped trailing whitespace but we discovered it did not canonicalize dynamic tokens (UUIDs, timestamps). The cache key still included the raw prompt in some code paths.

liam: Confirmed. In traces there's a hot path where `normalize_prefix_key` returns before applying `strip_dynamic_fragments`. Essentially we hashed pre-normalized string. That leads to near-unique keys and continuous evictions. I can reproduce locally with the harness.

support-bot: Support note: customer logs included repeated entries: `kv_get miss key=<long_prompt_hash> pod=acme-prod-3 request_id=...` at 2026-03-10T06:32:14Z — repeated 10k times in 2m.

eva: Immediate mitigations: 1) pin hot prefixes for Acme on their dedicated pool (pre-warm their top N prompts), 2) temporarily bump prefix cache size on their pod from 8k -> 32k, 3) enable soft-TTL eviction (avoid strict LRU churn). I'll open a fast rollback/rollout.

jamal: Also propose routing policy change: when miss_rate > 30% for a customer, route to smaller model variant or a degraded path to keep p99 lower while we fix. Cuts token latency and keeps users online.

liam: Local patch ready. Fix is to ensure `normalize_prefix_key` always runs `strip_dynamic_fragments(prompt)` before hashing. Small diff. With patch + cache bump my repro drops p99 from 12s -> ~650ms. I'll push to staging and run smoke tests.

ops-jen: Rolling fix to staging now. Quick repro runner we used: `python tools/repro_prefix_thrash.py --clients 200 --seq_len 64 --unique_prefixes 10000` — produces the same miss/eviction pattern.

cami: Customer-side workaround while we deploy: change templating to remove user identifiers from prompt or pass them as metadata (so prompts remain cacheable). We documented steps in the support ticket.

jamal: Good. ETA for prod rollout?

liam: If staging passes, ~1 hour. We'll monitor eviction_rate and p99. Plan: roll fix to canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with metric check gates. Add alert: eviction_rate > 0.05 or prefix_miss_rate > 0.25.

sre-bot: Deploy scheduled by liam in 1h. Monitoring: /alerts/kv-eviction-thrash and /dashboards/kv-prefix-heatmap.

support-bot: Ticket updated with repro, mitigation steps, and ETA. Customer accepted temporary warmup and will hold changes on their templating until we confirm.

jamal: Thanks everyone. I'll write up an incident summary + timeline after prod is stable.
